instantiated_cells.justification: A "legislative agent" is anyone engaged (employed/retained for compensation, defined broadly as any salary/payment/thing of value) to actively advocate as one of their main purposes — there is no dollar threshold, so any compensation triggers registration.
The statutory definition of "legislative agent" is based on being engaged for compensation to actively advocate; no lobbyist-side expenditure threshold is used in the definition.

The definition uses a qualitative "main purposes" standard ("engaged during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes") rather than a quantitative time threshold.

Itemized reporting of meal and food/beverage expenditures to a particular official is required only when cumulative payments during a calendar year exceed $50, establishing a $50 per-official itemization de minimis for food/beverage expenditures.

Registration and updated statements (with accompanying expenditure statements) are required of every legislative agent and employer upon engagement, with no dollar threshold exempting low-spend entities from filing.
Ohio's lobbyist definition uses a qualitative "main purposes" test and the registration/filing duties in §101.72 contain no percentage-of-compensated-time exemption from filing.

content.text:
I'll analyze each question against the Ohio statute text.

**Row 001 - Compensation threshold for lobbyist registration:** §101.70(F) defines "legislative agent" as anyone "engaged during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes." §101.70(H) defines "engage" as being "employed or retained for compensation." No dollar threshold — any compensation triggers it.

**Row 002 - Expenditure threshold for lobbyist definition:** The definition is based on compensation/engagement, not on lobbyist spending. No expenditure threshold exists in the definition.

**Row 003 - Time standard in definition:** §101.70(F) requires "actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — qualitative ("main purposes"), not a quantitative time threshold.

**Row 004 - Per-item itemization threshold:** §101.73(B)(3) requires itemization of meals/food/beverages only when cumulative payments exceed $50 per calendar year per official. For other expenditures under (B)(2), itemization is required whenever made (no de minimis).

**Row 005 - Overall filing-exemption threshold:** No de minimis exemption from filing exists — registration and filing are required upon engagement regardless of amount.

**Row 006 - Time-percent exemption from filing:** No percentage-of-time threshold exists for filing exemption.
